chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Pray facing the side of the Prophet's grave (peace be upon him and his family), even if the prayer of the believer reaches him wherever they are.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on facing the Prophet's grave during prayer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the practice of *Qiblatayn* (facing the side of the Prophet's grave) as a recommended act of reverence (*Ihtiram*) rather than obligatory worship (*Ibadah*), distinguishing it from the primary Qibla of the Kaaba. The Imam clarifies that the spiritual efficacy of the prayer reaches the Prophet regardless of the believer's distance, emphasizing the metaphysical connection between the faithful and the Ahl al-Bayt. This ruling is central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the etiquette of prayer in the presence of the Prophet's tomb in Medina.
